chunk_text: Quick catch is a player shortcut during a wild encounter. The help center does not list it as a control, and a client update can remove it. Hold the berry button so the berry list stays open. With another finger, throw the ball. While the ball is still in the air, release the berry button and tap the flee button. The game returns you to the map and still resolves the throw. A successful catch completes in the background. A break-out opens the encounter again without the long catch animation, so the next throw starts sooner. The shortcut does not raise the catch rate. Curveballs, a smaller catch ring, and berries still decide whether the Pokemon stays in the ball.

chunk_text: Candy XL belongs to one evolutionary family, the same way regular Candy does. Trainers start receiving it at Trainer level 31. It can drop from catching, transferring, hatching an egg, evolving, trading, feeding a berry to a Gym defender, walking a buddy, and catching after a raid. Most of those are a chance, not a guaranteed stack. Catching an evolved Pokemon, or a Legendary, Mythical, or Ultra Beast, tends to award more Candy XL than catching a basic Pokemon. A higher-level wild Pokemon also improves the odds on a normal catch. Pinap Berries multiply regular catch Candy. They do not multiply Candy XL.
title: Where Candy XL comes from

chunk_text: Regular Candy converts into Candy XL at 100 Candy for 1 Candy XL. The trade is one way: Candy XL does not convert back into Candy. Open the Pokemon, open its candy menu, and choose the Candy XL conversion. Convert only a surplus. That family still needs regular Candy for evolutions, a second Charged Attack, and other unlocks. Rare Candy XL, from the item bag, becomes 1 Candy XL for the family you apply it to. Candy XL is what powering up past level 40 spends, together with Stardust. The power-up button shows the cost before you spend it.

chunk_text: While a Mega Evolution is active, catching a Pokemon that shares a type with that Mega awards extra Candy. The match is a shared type, not a type that is super effective against the catch. A Dark and Steel catch wants a Dark Mega or a Steel Mega. A Fighting Mega does not earn the bonus just because Fighting is super effective. Use the Mega form's types when they differ from the base form. The bonus lasts for the Mega Evolution period, not only for the moment you Mega Evolve. The Pokemon's own Mega screen lists the candy and Candy XL bonus for the level that individual has reached. Read that screen if the numbers matter, because a later level can change them.

chunk_text: Mega Level belongs to one Pokemon, not the whole species. Mega Evolving that same Pokemon again raises its level. The public feature guide describes three levels. Base adds 1 catch Candy for a shared type. High still adds 1 catch Candy, adds a catch XP bonus, and gives a great chance at extra Candy XL, described there as 10 percent. Max adds 2 catch Candy, a larger XP bonus, and an excellent Candy XL chance, described there as 25 percent. Higher levels also shorten the rest period before that Pokemon can Mega Evolve again and lower the Mega Energy cost. A further level can exist beyond those three. The bonuses printed on that Pokemon's Mega screen are the ones in effect.

chunk_text: A trade awards Candy for the evolutionary family of the Pokemon you receive. Candy XL from a trade is a chance until the two Pokemon were caught far apart, and a long distance makes Candy XL likely or guaranteed. The trade screen shows the Candy before you confirm, so read that preview instead of guessing. Special trades, such as a Legendary, a shiny, or a Pokemon that would be new to the Pokedex, are limited per day. Trading is a poor way to farm Candy compared with catching during a bonus, and it spends the Pokemon you send away. Distance is measured between the catch locations, not between where the two trainers are standing.

chunk_text: A Community Day or another catch event can list its own candy bonus, such as extra catch Candy, a higher Candy XL chance, or a shorter egg distance. Those bonuses come from the live event listing, not from this guide. The Mega catch bonus stacks with an event bonus in the usual way: Mega Evolve a Pokemon that shares a type with the featured species, at the highest Mega Level you can, and leave it Mega Evolved while you catch. Do not Mega Evolve a counter type. A type that hits the featured species super effectively is the right choice for a raid, and the wrong choice for catch candy. If the event listing names the species, use that species' types for the shared-type check.

chunk_text: A Pinap Berry used before a successful catch multiplies that catch's regular Candy. A Silver Pinap Berry also multiplies regular Candy and makes the catch easier than a plain Pinap. Neither berry multiplies Candy XL. Berries, curveballs, and a smaller catch ring change the catch itself. They do not change which Mega type earns the catch-candy bonus. Feed the berry, then throw. If you are also using the quick catch shortcut, the berry still has to be applied before the ball is thrown, because the shortcut only skips the catch animation.
